Below is a quick‑start guide on how to pull the comment list for a specific domain (e.g., **apple.com**) using your **Delta key**. I’ll cover the most common ways to do this: | Method | What you’ll need | How to call it | |--------|------------------|----------------| | **HTTP GET** (raw) | • Your `delta_key` (string)
• Base URL of the Delta API (`https://api.delta.com/v1/` or your custom endpoint)
• Optional query params (`limit`, `offset`, etc.) | `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer " https://api.delta.com/v1/domains/apple.com/comments` | | **Python `requests`** | Same as above + `pip install requests` | See code snippet below | | **Delta SDK** (if you’re using one) | Install the SDK (`pip install delta-sdk`) | `client = DeltaClient(api_key="YOUR_DELTA_KEY")\ncomments = client.get_comments(domain="apple.com")` | --- ## 1. Using a raw HTTP GET request ```bash curl -X GET \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_DELTA_KEY" \ "https://api.delta.com/v1/domains/apple.com/comments" ``` *Replace `YOUR_DELTA_KEY` with the actual key you received when you signed up.* ### Optional query parameters | Parameter | Description | Example | |-----------|-------------|---------| | `limit` | Max number of comments to return (default 100) | `?limit=50` | | `offset` | Pagination offset | `?offset=200` | | `sort` | Sort order (`asc` or `desc`) | `?sort=desc` | Example with pagination: ```bash curl -X GET \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_DELTA_KEY" \ "https://api.delta.com/v1/domains/apple.com/comments?limit=20&offset=40" ``` --- ## 2. Using Python (`requests`) ```python import requests API_BASE = "https://api.delta.com/v1" DOMAIN = "apple.com" DELTA_KEY = "YOUR_DELTA_KEY" headers = { "Authorization": f"Bearer {DELTA_KEY}", "Accept": "application/json", } params = { "limit": 50, # optional "offset": 0, # optional "sort": "desc", # optional } response = requests.get(f"{API_BASE}/domains/{DOMAIN}/comments", headers=headers, params=params) if response.status_code == 200: data = response.json() # `data` will contain fields like `comments`, `total_count`, etc. print(data) else: print(f"Error {response.status_code}: {response.text}") ``` **What you’ll see in the JSON response** ```json { "total_count": 1234, "comments": [ { "id": "cmt_001", "author": "John Doe", "text": "Great product!", "created_at": "2024-10-01T12:34:56Z" }, ... ] } ``` --- ## 3. Using the Delta SDK (if available) If you’re already using the official Delta SDK, the call is even simpler: ```python from delta_sdk import DeltaClient client = DeltaClient(api_key="YOUR_DELTA_KEY") comments_response = client.get_comments(domain="apple.com", limit=50, offset=0) print(comments_response) ``` The SDK handles authentication, pagination helpers, and error handling for you. --- ## Common pitfalls & troubleshooting | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | **401 Unauthorized** | Double‑check that you’re using the correct key and that it’s still active. | | **404 Not Found** | Verify that the domain (`apple.com`) is registered in your Delta account. | | **Rate limiting (429)** | Add exponential back‑off or reduce request frequency. | | **Unexpected JSON structure** | Inspect the raw response (`response.text`) to see if the API has changed. | --- ### Quick sanity check Try running the following minimal test to confirm your key works: ```bash curl -X GET \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_DELTA_KEY" \ "https://api.delta.com/v1/domains/apple.com/comments?limit=1" ``` If you get a JSON payload with at least one comment, you’re all set! --- Let me know if you hit any errors or if you’d like help automating pagination or filtering by date. Happy coding!
